title: HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund for Non-Local Students
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund scholarships support outstanding first-year non-local undergraduates, with targeted awards for students from Belt and Road countries/regions (e.g. Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar, Mongolia) - full funding from the government, separate from CityUHK's own schemes.

## Question

Can a non-local student get a government (HKSAR) scholarship for CityUHK CS?

## Answer

Yes, via the **HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund** - a government scheme (not a CityUHK one) that supports outstanding non-local students pursuing undergraduate studies in Hong Kong. Key points from CityUHK's pages:

- Aimed at **first-year full-time** UGC-funded programme students.
- **Targeted scholarships** are made available to students from **countries/regions along the Belt and Road**, such as **Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar and Mongolia** (other nationalities can also appear under the broader Fund, including 'Belt & Road' and non-academic-award/talent-development categories).
- Awards are administered through the government fund with CityUHK handling nominations - check the current Fund guidelines on the HKSAR fund's official site for amounts and eligibility, since the Fund's rules are set by the government and updated per cycle.
- Recipients appear alongside CityUHK's own scholarships in department award lists (e.g. BMS 2025/26 lists HKSAR Government Scholarship and Belt & Road Scholarship recipients), so a CS student can realistically be on this list.

It is **separate from and in addition to** CityUHK's own Entrance Scholarship Scheme - but government-fund rules may limit stacking, so confirm with both the Fund and the University for your nationality and year.

## Examples

- A first-year JS1204 student from Thailand may be considered for the targeted Belt & Road scholarship under the Fund in parallel with CityUHK's Half Tuition entrance scholarship - the combination is confirmed through the University's nomination process.

title: How to Apply for CityUHK Entrance Scholarships (No Application Needed)
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> You do not apply. Flagship, Institutional and Dean's Scholarships are awarded automatically from your JUPAS application and HKDSE results; eligible students are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date (4 August 2027).

## Question

Do I need to submit a separate scholarship application when applying to CityUHK CS?

## Answer

No. The official notes state: **no application is required** for Flagship, Institutional and Dean's Scholarships. Eligibility is assessed automatically from your JUPAS registration (which programme you registered) and your HKDSE results, and eligible students are **notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round Offers announcement date** (per the JUPAS calendar - **4 August 2027** for the 2027 cycle).

Practical points:
- Make sure your **email address on JUPAS is current** before mid-August - the award notice comes by email.
- For **non-JUPAS** local entrants, the same no-application rule applies; eligible students are notified 'in due course'.
- If you are offered more than one scholarship, only the **highest amount** is awarded.
- The schemes target **newly admitted students**; in special circumstances the University may consider re-admission candidates.
- Questions: CityUHK scholarship details line **+852 3442 8152** (admission matters: +852 3442 9094).

## Examples

- A student admitted to JS1204 on 4 August 2027 with three 5** subjects checks their email the same day and finds the Institutional Scholarship notification (HK$59,000/yr) attached to the offer.
- No form, no interview, no separate form fee - the scholarship is decided from the data you already submitted to JUPAS.

title: Institutional Scholarships for JUPAS Entrants
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> For local JUPAS entrants incl. JS1204/JS1218 (not flagships), per year: 4 subjects at 5** = HK$69,000; 3 subjects at 5** = HK$59,000; 2 subjects at 5** and scholarship score >= 25 = HK$35,000; each tier also gives a one-off HK$25,000 exchange scholarship. All 5** in one sitting; M1/M2 count (both = one subject). **Scale: 5\*\*=8.5, 5\*=7, 5=5.5, 4=4, 3=3; score = 3 core (excl. CSDDD) + 2 best electives.**

## Question

How much is the Institutional Scholarship for a local JUPAS student admitted to BSc Computer Science or Cybersecurity?

## Answer

Institutional Scholarships apply to local JUPAS entrants in **any government-funded programme except the ten flagship programmes** - so they cover **JS1204 BSc Computer Science** and **JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity** (and all other standard programmes). Tiers for 2027 entry, based on HKDSE results **obtained in one sitting** (repeat subjects do not count):

| Criteria | Value (per annum) | Exchange scholarship |
|---|---|---|
| 4 subjects or more with 5** and Level 4 or above in either Chinese or English | **HK$69,000** | HK$25,000 (one-off) |
| 3 subjects with 5** and Level 4 or above in either Chinese or English | **HK$59,000** | HK$25,000 (one-off) |
| 2 subjects with 5**, Level 4+ in Chinese or English, and HKDSE scholarship score >= 25 | **HK$35,000** | HK$25,000 (one-off) |

Rules to know:
- **Category A subjects and Mathematics extended modules (M1/M2) count** as the '5**' subjects; if you took both M1 and M2 they count as **one** subject.
- If **English** is used to count toward a '5**', you must have Level 4 or above in **Chinese** (and vice versa).
- The 'score >= 25' for the lowest tier uses the **scholarship scoring scale** (see [[Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale]]).
- Duration: **4 to 6 years** depending on the normal duration of the registered programme (JS1204/JS1218 = 4 years).
- Renewed automatically each year on achieving the specified CGPA by the end of Semester B.
- **No application is required** - eligible students are notified by email on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date.

## Examples
- **Worked example (top tier):** English 5**, Chinese 5**, Maths 5**, M1 5*, ICT 5, History 4, all in one sitting. Three subjects at 5** and Level 4+ in both languages -> **HK$69,000/yr** x 4 = HK$276,000 + one-off HK$25,000 exchange scholarship (~HK$301,000 total against ~HK$188,000 tuition).
- **Worked example (middle tier):** English 5**, Maths 5**, M1 5*, ICT 5, Chinese 4, History 4. Two 5** subjects; score = core (4 + 8.5 + 8.5 = 21) + electives (7 + 5.5) = 33.5 >= 25 -> **HK$35,000/yr** x 4 = HK$140,000 + HK$25,000 one-off exchange.
- **English/Chinese cross-rule:** if English is one of the 5** subjects used, Chinese must be Level 4 or above (and vice versa); otherwise that 5** does not count toward the tier.
- **M1/M2 rule:** extended modules count as 5** subjects, but M1 + M2 together count as ONE subject. Repeated subjects are not counted; all results must be from one sitting.

title: Institutional Scholarships for Non-JUPAS Entrants
text:

> Local non-JUPAS entrants (high-school 2027 graduates) in non-flagship programmes, e.g. JS1204 (1561A): GCE A-Level 4A* or IB >= 41 => HK$69,000/yr; 2A*+1A or IB 38-40 => HK$59,000/yr; 1A*+2A or IB 36-37 => HK$35,000/yr - each with one-off HK$25,000 exchange scholarship.

## Question

What entrance scholarship can a local non-JUPAS IB / A-Level student get for BSc Computer Science (1561A)?

## Answer

Local non-JUPAS entrants graduating from high school in 2027 and admitted to **any programme except the ten flagship ones** (so including **BSc Computer Science, code 1561A**) are eligible for the Institutional Scholarships on these criteria:

| Criteria (GCE A-Level / IB Diploma incl. bonus points) | Value per annum | Exchange scholarship |
|---|---|---|
| 4A*  /  IB >= 41 | **HK$69,000** | HK$25,000 (one-off) |

Same rules as the JUPAS version: **all scores in one sitting**, repeat subjects not counted, two AS = one A-Level, the same subject not counted at both levels, **GCE Chinese not counted**, and non-flagship-only (an ACT/1070 entrant uses the Flagship tier instead). Tenable for 4-6 years (4 for JS1204), renewed on CGPA. No application required.

## Examples

- A local A-Level student admitted to JS1204 (1561A) with 4A* (e.g. Maths, Further Maths, Physics, ICT) receives HK$69,000/yr x 4 + HK$25,000 one-off exchange scholarship.

title: Non-Local Tuition and Living Costs at CityUHK
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> Non-local (international) students pay about HK$190,000 per academic year tuition (2026/27), a HK$15,000 acceptance fee, and living costs of about HK$50,000-60,000/year - which is what the international entrance scholarships (Top/Full/Half tuition) offset.

## Question

What does studying BSc CS at CityUHK actually cost an international student?

## Answer

Official non-local figures for 2026/27 entry (admission fees-and-scholarships page):

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| **Application fee** | HK$450 (up to 3 programme choices) |
| **Acceptance fee** | HK$15,000 (non-refundable, credited toward tuition) |
| **Tuition fee** | **HK$190,000 per academic year** |
| **Living costs** | HK$50,000-60,000 per academic year |
| **Accommodation** | Student residence: HK$20,800 for two semesters; off-campus: HK$50,000-60,000 |

So a four-year JS1204 degree without scholarship is roughly **HK$760,000 tuition + ~HK$220,000 living** before books and travel - and this is why the **Entrance Scholarship Scheme** (Top: HK$210,000/yr covering tuition + university-managed accommodation + partial living expenses; Full Tuition; Half Tuition) is the headline decision factor for international applicants. The same acceptance fee is HK$5,000 for local students, who pay about HK$47,000/yr tuition instead.

## Examples

- A Top Scholarship recipient's four-year out-of-pocket cost drops to roughly living expenses not covered by the allowance - versus ~HK$980,000+ for an unaided international student.
- The HK$15,000 acceptance fee is credited toward tuition on enrolment, so it is not purely 'lost' money.

title: Other Donor Scholarships and Prizes at CityUHK
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> CityUHK offers 120+ donor-funded scholarships and prizes (e.g. HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship HK$50,000, Li Po Chun, Mapletree, AIA, Chi-Li Pao, Li Dak Sum Yip Yio Chin) for current students - separate from and stackable with the university-wide entrance scholarships.

## Question

Besides the entrance scholarships, what other money can a CityUHK student earn during their degree?

## Answer

Thanks to donor funding, CityUHK offers **more than 120 scholarships, prizes and academic awards** at undergraduate (and postgraduate) levels. Well-known ones visible in department award lists (e.g. Biomedical Sciences 2025/26) include:

- **HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship** - funded by the Hongkong Bank Foundation for outstanding UGC-funded full-time **local** undergraduates (academic excellence + community involvement + communication); **HK$50,000 per recipient**.
- **Li Po Chun Charitable Trust Fund Scholarships** (undergraduate), **Mapletree Scholarships**, **AIA Scholarships**, **Chi-Li Pao Foundation Scholarships for Academic Outstanding Students**, **Li Dak Sum Yip Yio Chin Outstanding Student Scholarship**, **Ms Ada Chow Scholarships**, **Pao Ho Mei Chun Scholarships**, **CityU Scholarship / CityUHK Scholarship**, **Link University Scholarship**, **Lee Shau Kee Scholarships for Academic Outstanding Students**.
- **Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarships for Local Students** and the **Residence Scholarship Scheme for Student Athletes** for local athletes.
- **Student Development Scholarships**, **CMA and Donors Scholarships**, and department-specific awards (the College of Business, for instance, adds its own entrance scholarships of HK$20,000-40,000 one-off for BSc Computational Finance and Financial Technology and BBA Global Business).

Most are **for current students** (i.e. applied for after admission, often via department/SDS nomination on academic merit) and are **not subject to the 'no concurrent awards' rule** that binds the Flagship/Institutional/Dean's tiers - so a JS1204 Institutional Scholar recipient can still be an HSBC or Li Po Chun recipient in later years. The full list is maintained by Student Development Services.

## Examples

- A JS1204 student who received the Dean's Tier 1 entrance award can be nominated for the HSBC Hong Kong Scholarship in Year 2 (HK$50,000, one of the most competitive donor awards) - the two awards coexist.
- The College of Business entrance scholarship (HK$20,000-40,000 one-off) is an example of a unit-level award layered on top of the university-wide tiers for eligible majors.

title: Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship for Non-Local Students
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> Outstanding non-local (international/continental-level) student athletes can get the Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship - HK$200,000 per year covering tuition and partial living expenses - via the Student Athletes Admission Scheme (SAAS).

## Question

Is there a scholarship route for international student athletes?

## Answer

Yes. CityUHK's **Student Athletes Admission Scheme (SAAS)** (run since 1997; 1,200+ student athletes admitted) provides admission and scholarships for outstanding non-local student athletes. The headline award is the **Outstanding Athletes Entrance Scholarship (OAES) for Non-Local Students**:

- **HK$200,000 per annum** for athletes at **International / Continental level** - covering **tuition and partial living expenses**.
- There are also athlete-entrance awards at lower competition levels and **Residence Scholarship Scheme for Student Athletes** components (hall place), with local student-athlete awards under the same umbrella.

Eligibility is set by competition level and the SAAS selection process; applications run through Student Development Services (SDS), with nomination forms on the CityUHK athletics page. This is a separate track from the academic Entrance Scholarship Scheme - a student who enters through SAAS gets the athletes' awards rather than being stacked onto the academic Top/Full/Half tiers.

## Examples

- An international-level athlete admitted to JS1204 through SAAS with the OAES pays no tuition plus receives a living allowance of up to HK$200,000/yr - comparable in value to the academic Top Scholarship but with the entry route going through the athletes' admission process.

title: Scholarship HKDSE Scoring Scale (How Scholarship Scores Are Calculated)
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> A different scale from JUPAS level points: 5** = 8.5, 5* = 7, 5 = 5.5, 4 = 4, 3 = 3, 2 = 2, 1 = 1. Score = 3 core subjects (excluding Citizenship and Social Development) + 2 best electives; best attempt used if repeated. E.g. 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 27.5.

## Question

How is the 'HKDSE score' in the scholarship tables calculated, and is it the same as my JUPAS score?

## Answer

It is **not** the same as the JUPAS admission score. Scholarship thresholds use CityU's own **scoring scale** for HKDSE Category A core and elective subjects (including M1/M2):

| Level | Score |
|---|---|
| 5** | **8.5** |
| 5* | **7** |
| 5 | **5.5** |
| 4 | **4** |
| 3 | **3** |
| 2 | **2** |
| 1 | **1** |

The score adds **3 core subjects (excluding 'Citizenship and Social Development') + the 2 electives with the best results**. If a subject was attempted more than once, the best result is used. Category C other-language subjects (Japanese, Korean, French/German/Spanish, Urdu) also have a scale (e.g. Japanese N1 = 7, Korean Level 6 = 7, French/German/Spanish C1 = 5.5) for use as electives.

Compare with the JUPAS level-point table (5** = 8, 5* = 7, 5 = 5, 4 = 4...) used for admission scores - the scholarship scale pays more for top grades (8.5 for 5**).

## Examples
- **27.5 (Flagship full / Dean's Tier 1 threshold):** 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 8.5 + 5.5 + 5.5 + 4 + 4.
- **30.5 (LLB threshold):** 5* + 5* + 5* + 5 + 4 = 7 + 7 + 7 + 5.5 + 4.
- **25 (Dean's Tier 2 / Institutional entry):** 5* + 5 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 7 + 5.5 + 5.5 + 4 + 3.
- **Category C language electives** score on their own scale but map to the same values: Japanese N1 = 7, Korean Level 6 = 7, French/German/Spanish C1 = 5.5 - so a Japanese N1 elective counts the same as a 5* for the scholarship score.
- **Vs the JUPAS admission score:** the same 5** + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 profile is a JUPAS level-point score of 8 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 4 = 26 (weight 1) but a **scholarship score of 27.5** - always recompute; never reuse the JUPAS number for a scholarship threshold.

- [[JS1204 2026 JUPAS Score Formula]]

title: Scholarship Renewal and CGPA Requirements
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> Institutional and Dean's Scholarships renew automatically each year only if the student achieves a specified CGPA by the end of Semester B; Flagship Scholarships renew on continuing in the flagship programme. Non-local entrance scholarships also renew on CGPA. The exact CGPA figures are not published.

## Question

What must a scholarship recipient do to keep the scholarship every year?

## Answer

The renewals are **automatic but conditional** - no re-application, but the conditions must be met by the end of **Semester B** each year:

| Scholarship | Annual renewal condition |
|---|---|
| **Institutional** (JUPAS and non-JUPAS local) | Achieve the **specified CGPA** |
| **Dean's** | Achieve the **specified CGPA** |
| **Flagship** | **Continue studying in the flagship programme** (i.e. do not transfer out of e.g. ACT) |
| **International Entrance Scheme** (Top / Full / Half) | Attain the **minimum required CGPA each year** throughout the period of study |

CityU's page does not publish the exact CGPA thresholds - it says 'a specified Cumulative Grade Point Average'. In practice these operate as academic-progress conditions, so a serious drop in grades can end the award. Note CityU's own undergraduate Dean's List uses SGPA 3.7+ as the bar for outstanding standing, which gives a sense of the scale - but for your specific award, the CGPA requirement stated in your award letter governs.

Duration is also capped: awards run for the normal duration of the registered programme (4 years for JS1204/JS1218, up to 5-6 for longer programmes such as JS1221).

## Examples

- A JS1221 Dean's Tier 1 recipient keeps HK$94,000/yr for up to the programme's duration provided the CGPA condition is met by the end of each Semester B.
- An ACT Flagship recipient who transfers out of the flagship programme loses the Flagship renewal from that point.

title: Scholarship Timeline 2027 (JUPAS Entrants)
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> 2027 cycle: HKDSE results 14 July; reprioritisation 14-16 July; JUPAS Main Round offers (and scholarship notifications by email) 4 August; enrolment mid-August; upgraded-results offers 19 August; Semester A starts 30 August.

## Question

When exactly will a JUPAS applicant know whether they got a CityUHK scholarship in 2027?

## Answer

Per the official 'important dates for JUPAS entrants' (2027, subject to changes), the scholarship decision arrives **on the JUPAS Main Round offer announcement date**: the same email that carries your programme offer states any Flagship / Institutional / Dean's award, since no separate application exists.

| Date (2027) | Event |
|---|---|
| **Wed 14 July** | Release of 2027 HKDSE results |
| **Wed-Fri 14-16 July** | JUPAS programme-choice reprioritisation |
| **Wed 4 August** | **JUPAS Main Round offers announced** - scholarship awards notified by email on this date |
| **Mid August** | Enrolment |
| **Late August** | Student orientation |
| **Thu 19 August** | Offers for applicants with **upgraded HKDSE results** announced (an upgrade can change which scholarship tier applies) |
| **Mon 30 August** | Semester A 2027/28 starts |

Strategy note: because scholarships are assigned from your results and your **registered** programme choices, reprioritising in mid-July (e.g. putting a flagship programme like ACT JS1070 ahead of JS1204) can change which award pool you fall into - Flagship tiers for JS1070 vs Institutional/Dean's tiers for JS1204 - at no extra cost, since you don't apply separately.

Contact for scholarship queries: **+852 3442 8152** (admission matters: +852 3442 9094).

## Examples

- A student who reprioritises JS1070 above JS1204 on 15 July and is admitted to JS1070 with score 27.5 learns on 4 August that they hold the ACT Flagship full scholarship (100% tuition + hall fees), not the Institutional tier.
- A student whose HKDSE results are upgraded after the main round gets a new offer (and possibly a different scholarship tier) on 19 August.

title: What Do Flagship Scholarship Recipients Get (Benefits)
text:
> [!tip] Short answer
> 
> Beyond the money: guaranteed hall berth, exchange sponsorships up to HK$500,000 (one-off), overseas exchanges, Global Work Attachment Programme, dedicated academic mentorship and early research engagement, Golden Key Club membership, and the Service Leadership Training Programme.

## Question

What non-cash benefits come with a CityUHK scholarship?

## Answer

CityUHK scholarship recipients (CityUHK Scholarships for Hong Kong Talents) receive a package of learning and advancement opportunities, on top of the tuition/hall-fee award:

- **Guaranteed berth in the halls of residence** - for **Flagship Scholarship recipients** (not automatic for Institutional/Dean's recipients).
- **Exchange sponsorships** - up to **HK$500,000 one-off** for Flagship recipients; **HK$25,000 one-off** for Institutional recipients.
- **Global experience through overseas exchanges** - outbound student exchange opportunities.
- **Global Work Attachment Programme (GWAP)** - work-experience attachment with organisations abroad.
- **Academic mentorship** - dedicated academic development and/or early engagement in academic research.
- **Golden Key Club membership** - an all-round development platform and network for scholarship recipients.
- **Service Leadership Training Programme** - service-learning platform for engaging with society.

These benefits matter for cost-of-living decisions: a Flagship recipient's hall fees are covered (double room occupancy) and their hall place is guaranteed - relevant for students who would otherwise need off-campus accommodation (HK$50,000-60,000/year).

## Examples

- An ACT Flagship recipient in Year 1 gets a double hall berth at no cost (hall fees covered by the 100% award), a guaranteed place every year, and access to exchange sponsorship - a material saving versus a non-scholarship student paying ~HK$20,800+ for a student residence per semester.
- An Institutional Scholar recipient (JS1204) gets the HK$25,000 one-off exchange scholarship but must secure a hall place through the normal residence allocation.

title: CityUHK CS Admission FAQ
text: A plain-language FAQ for **City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK) — Department of Computer Science** undergraduate admission: **400+ interlinked notes** on the three majors, JUPAS scoring, published scores 2023–2026, the new 1.5× weighting policy, non-JUPAS routes, curriculum, programmes, internships, scholarships, and careers. Open the 🧮 What's My Score? calculator to try your score live. > [!warning] Disclaimer > > Most content of this page is generated by AI. It may occasionally be inaccurate or based on pages that are not yet up to date. For definitive information, please consult the official CityUHK sources. ## The three majors | Major | Summary | Intake 2026/27 | 2026 score | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **BSc Computer Science [JS1204](/05_programmes/js1204-bsc-computer-science-overview.html)** | Flagship 4-year CS with **5 streams** (AI, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Multimedia, Software Engineering), **internship: 9 months at a company, or 160 hours of industry/research work + 3 CS electives**, HKIE-accredited | ~85 local | median **23** | | **BSc Cybersecurity [JS1218](/05_programmes/js1218-bsc-cybersecurity-overview.html)** | 4-year degree for the cybersecurity talent gap (System/Software Security, Cryptography, Privacy, Cyber Risk), same Year-3 internship option as JS1204 | ~29 local | median **20.5** | | **Double degrees [JS1221](/05_programmes/js1221-double-degree-overview.html) / [JS1063](/05_programmes/js1063-llb-and-bsccs-double-degree-overview.html)** | 5-year CS + Computational Finance & FinTech / CS (AI) + Law, same Year-3 internship option as JS1204 — **only ~10 places**, JUPAS only | ~10–18 local | median **23** | --- ## Q1 — What makes these majors attractive? {#q1} - **Direct admission to the major** — students join Computer Science or Cybersecurity directly, not a broad "department" where seats are re-allocated. - **5 streams inside CS** (AI / Cybersecurity / Data Science / Multimedia / Software Engineering) — one major, many specialisations. - **Industry internship built into Year 3** (Q2) — every student completes an internship: 9-month, or 160 hours with 3 extra CS electives. Applies to all CS majors (JS1204, JS1218, JS1221, JS1063). - **97.5% full-time employment** of BSc CS graduates (2024 survey); HKIE accreditation (first CS programme in HK). - Joint Bachelor's with **Columbia University** (direct Year-1 admission from 2026/27). **Read:** [[JS1204 BSc Computer Science Overview]] · [[JS1218 BSc Cybersecurity Overview]] · [[CS Study Streams Explained]] ## Q2 — The industry internship: arrangement and why it matters {#q2} - **Year 3, credit-bearing, at real companies/government** — after two full years of study. Two routes (2026/27 onwards): **CS3505 IT Professional Internship** (9 months, 9 CU) or **CS3000** Professional Career Development Internship (160 hours) + 3 extra CS electives. Same option across JS1204, JS1218, JS1221 and JS1063. - For the 9-month internship: works **4 days a week with Fridays off for classes** — it runs alongside study, it doesn't pause the degree. - Jointly assessed by a CityU supervisor **and** the employer; a deliberate differentiator vs programmes where internships are optional. **Read:** [[IT Professional Internship Overview]] · [[Why the Industry Internship Matters]] · [[Internship Employers and Participating Companies]] ## Q3 — Main courses and how they are arranged {#q3} - 4-year degree (~120 CU) in four layers: **Gateway Education → College courses (programming from Year 1) → Calculus/Linear Algebra → CS core + electives**. - Year 1 (33 CU) already includes programming (CS1302A), Computer Organisation, and computational probability modelling. - Students either complete 3 stream courses to fulfil a study-stream requirement, or pick electives freely across streams. **Read:** [[Curriculum of BSc Computer Science]] · [[CS Core Courses Explained]] · [[CS First Year Courses and Credits]] ## Q4 — How is the JUPAS score calculated? {#q4} - **Best 5 DSE subjects** (Category A, excluding CSD and Liberal Studies), **all weight 1** in the published 2026 formula. - 2026: **median 23, lower quartile 22** (JS1204); Cybersecurity 20.5. - Minimum entrance: Eng 3, Chi 3, Math 3, CSD attained, **plus Level 3 in one of ICT / Physics / Chemistry / Biology / M1 / M2** and a second Level-3 elective. - 🧮 Try your score live in the What's My Score? calculator — enter your DSE grades for the base score, the 1.5× version, and where you sit vs the medians. **Read:** [[JS1204 2026 JUPAS Score Formula]] · [[Worked Example Computing JS1204 Admission Score]] · [[JUPAS Minimum Entrance Requirements for CS]] ## Q5 — 🆕 NEW: the 1.5× subject-weighting policy {#q5} - CityUHK is promoting a policy where **English, Mathematics, ICT, M1, M2, Physics, Chemistry and Biology count at 1.5×** level points — strongly rewarding the exact subjects a CS student takes. - Same profile, very different score under 1.5× (e.g. 5-5-5-4-4 in CS-relevant subjects: 24.5 → **36.75**). - ⚠️ The **published 2026 formula is still best-5 weight 1** — always confirm the current year's official formula before applying. **Read:** [[1.5x Subject Weighting Policy (Draft) Status]] · [[Subject Weightings in JUPAS Admission Scores]] ## Q6 — How competitive is it? Which bands get in? {#q6} - Most admitted students come from **Band A** (2026 median 23 ≈ 5-4-4-4-4+ profiles). - Around the **lower quartile (22)** is borderline (flexible admission may apply); **Bands D and E normally have no chance**. - Selection is **score-first**; bands are used as a tie-breaker. **Read:** [[Typical Admission Competitiveness Most Admits Come From Band A]] · [[JUPAS Band Choices Explained]] · [[How CityUHK Ranks Tied JUPAS Candidates]] ## Q7 — Is there a JUPAS interview? {#q7} - **No JUPAS interview is planned** — selection is by admission score. - Competition achievement
